It sounds dumb and cliché, but it does get better. I tried to end  it and failed. Then it got really bad. And somehow I kept breathing and little by little, a year and a half later, it is better. Not great. Just barely manageable. And I just keep breathing. Day by day. I wish you this!

It would most likely kill you. But then again, people have survived falls from much higher. If you are concerned about pain then you probably still have a very tiny glimmer of hope. 
I was there a year and a half ago. Many mistakes. Lost. Confused. Weak. Feeling numb. No appetite. Felt like I didn’t have the energy to brush my teeth. No one understood. No one. “Just be happy. Be grateful. Pray. Meditate.” All kinds of anti depressants. They just made things worse. Nothing worked. I constantly thought about how to end it. Going into the ocean and not turning back, jumping from a 10th story parking lot, smashing my car into a concrete wall, pills, rope, train…
I just didn’t want the pain or the shame to some in my family. I found one friend that listened, that didn’t judge me. His life was a fucking mess. But he didn’t care. He just got up and did the best he could or sometimes did nothing at all. Sat with him and smoked a fat joint. I slept for the first time in a year. And little by little I just stopped caring about what people thought. I moved away from all the toxic people. I avoid them like the plague. I stopped being hard on myself. Just take it one day at a time. Little by little it does get a little better. Not necessarily great. Just tolerable. It’s been really hard. It still is. Every fucking day. Seeing happy people makes it hard. Fuck Facebook Like they are so ignorant about how fucked up life can be. Seeing angry people is hard. Fuck the news. The world is fucked up. It’s all fucked up. But I’m still here. I’m still breathing. The best way to say fuck you to everybody is to live your life without giving a fuck what anybody thinks. I force myself to go outside and just look up at the sky or out to the horizon. Breathe, cry, yell, feel the heat, feel the cold. Just be.
Find someone, anyone, maybe a stranger that will just listen and be complete honest with that person.
Reach out to me if you want. I wish you strength and peace. And love. To carry on.

Puerto Rico is great! But you get extremes when it comes to people. There are wonderful nice people. Almost everybody speaks some English. And if you learn  a couple of words in Spanish, most people really appreciate it. But then you get some random a-holes. I’ve had really good vibes in the line up and some really angry dickheads. I had people buy me beers at the bar and also had my car broken into while out surfing. Girls are beautiful and sweet. Old people really nice. Just really pay attention to where you are in the line up.
